title: Usage-bracketed observability SKUs with contract questionnaire gating and premium SLA opt-in
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise customers frequently ask for longer observability retention windows and bundled compliance features (audit logs, encryption assurances) but we lack a standardized way to sell, gate, and operate these capabilities. Current product options are all-or-nothing (default retention + ad-hoc contracts). This experiment aims to test a repeatable packaging model that lets customers self-select increased retention and compliance bundles while allowing legal/ops to gate access via our security questionnaire/contract flow.

Hypothesis: Offering discrete, usage-bracketed observability SKUs (30d / 90d / 365d) and an optional Compliance Pack behind a short contract questionnaire will increase average ARR per enterprise account by >= 12% in pilot customers, with acceptable marginal cost (<5% uplift in token+storage cost) and low activation friction. The premium SLA opt-in (SLA 99.9% + 24/7 escalation) will convert ~10% of eligible enterprise customers.

Success metrics (primary):
- Pilot ARR uplift (delta ARR attributed to SKUs/add-ons)
- SKU activation rate for eligible customers
- Questionnaires completed / pass rate
- % of passes that convert to paid add-on within 30 days
- Marginal platform cost delta (tokens/storage/ingress)
- SLA opt-in rate and associated support load

Design / experiment plan:
1) SKU definitions (billing-friendly):
   - Observability-Core-30 (default): 30d retention, baseline alerts, included in default pricing
   - Observability-Extended-90: 90d retention + grouped retention access logs
   - Observability-Long-365: 365d retention + advanced audit export
   - Compliance-Pack: SOC2+ controls mapping doc + KMS integration checklist + quarterly compliance report (sold as add-on)
   - Premium-SLA: 99.9% uptime SLA + 24/7 escalation (+ price delta)
2) Usage brackets for pricing (monthly committed spend tiers): Small / Medium / Large; price multiplier scales with bandwidth/ingest band to keep per-unit economics sensible.
3) Contract questionnaire gating: short form (7 items) surfaced in Console when a tenant attempts to purchase Observability-Long-365 or Compliance-Pack. Questionnaire thresholds determine: auto-approve, manual-approve (legal review), auto-deny. Examples of questions: data residency required? KMS enabled? Contractual log retention clauses?
4) Entitlement flow: post-approve, entitlement toggled in Console & billing invoice rate adjusts next billing cycle. Manual-approve triggers an alert in Zendesk & Contract Ops.

Implementation notes / required work:
- PM: finalize SKU copy, pricing multipliers, pilot candidate list, contract questionnaire draft. (Owner: Leah)
- Engineering: Console UI for add-on purchase + questionnaire modal, billing integration for SKU rates, entitlement toggle API, telemetry for activation events. (Owner: ENG-42910 assigned team)
- Design: modal flows + in-console pricing summary + microcopy for questionnaire. (Owner: DES-2219)
- Legal/RevOps: draft T&Cs language for add-ons, playbook for manual approvals.
- Support/CS: run pilot outreach and onboarding checklist.

Rollout & timeline:
- Week 0-2: finalize SKU pricing and questionnaire (PM/Legal/RevOps)
- Week 2-4: console UI + billing hooks + design assets (ENG + Design)
- Week 4: internal dry run with Sales/CS; update docs (Confluence)
- Week 5-12: 8-week pilot with up to 5 enterprise customers (staggered start)
- Post-pilot (Week 12-14): analyze metrics, prepare decision doc for broader launch

Risk & mitigations: 
- Risk: High manual approval volume => mitigation: tune questionnaire auto-approve thresholds, add clear in-product messaging for expected review SLAs.
- Risk: Unexpected storage costs for 365d retention => mitigation: cap retention per tenant or introduce usage-band pricing to maintain margins.
- Risk: Legal complexity for compliance pack => mitigation: start with documentation + checklist rather than a fully contract-bound promise; require security_review_required true for Legal review.

Dependencies: integration with billing platform (ENG-42910), Console feature flags infrastructure (ENG-41107), Contract Ops playbook (PM-43144).

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/PM-49711+Observability+SKUs (draft)
- Design Figma flows: https://www.figma.com/file/observability-addons (internal)
- Billing PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1892

Notes: focus on low-friction self-serve for common enterprise needs while preserving manual control for high-risk entitlements.
